members: Methylphenidate: blocks DAT/NET אלוסטרית, has no effect on VMAT2 [1]
Dexmethylphenidate: the active D-enantiomer, twice as active as racemic D,L-MPH [1, 2]
Amphetamine: competitive inhibitor of DAT/NET, inhibits VMAT2 and reverses transporter direction [3]
Lisdexamfetamine: prodrug coupled with L-lysine, requires RBC enzymatic cleavage, reducing abuse potential [4]
drug_class.mechanism: Enhances DA and NE in synaptic cleft of Prefrontal Cortex (PFC), optimizing the signal-to-noise ratio via alpha-2A and D1 receptors [1, 5, 6]
kinetics: MPH half-life is ~5 hours [7, 8]; Amphetamine half-life is 10-12 hours [9]
Amphetamine metabolized primarily by CYP2D6 [10]; MPH by carboxylesterase CES1 [11]
Slow-release formulations occupancy of DAT is typically maintained below saturation at 50%-60% to avoid euphoria [12]

items: ADHD in children (6 years and older) and adolescents [16, 17]
ADHD Combined, Predominantly Inattentive, or Predominantly Hyperactive presentations [18]
Narcolepsy in children and adolescents (Dexmethylphenidate, D-Amphetamine, Lisdexamfetamine) [19-21]
Short-term stimulant response rate is ~70%, increasing to ~85% with sequential trials of both classes [22, 23]
key_numbers: 70% - response rate for single stimulant trial [22, 23]
85% - response rate after trying both classes sequentially [22, 23]
6 out of 9 - symptoms required for pediatric ADHD diagnosis (under age 17) [18]
5 out of 9 - symptoms required for diagnosis in age 17 and older [18]
12 - age before which symptoms must first manifest [18]

items: Appetite suppression and weight loss via DA/NE activity in hypothalamic hunger center [24]
Insomnia or delayed sleep onset (related to late-day dosing or evening rebound effect) [25]
Temporary growth deceleration in childhood, though expected adult height is eventually attained [24]
Moderate cardiovascular changes: increases in heart rate (3-10 bpm) and blood pressure (3-8 mmHg systolic, 2-14 mmHg diastolic) [25]
Zombie-like syndrome: cognitive overstimulation, flat affect, social withdrawal due to overdosage [26]
key_numbers: 3-10 bpm - average increase in resting heart rate [25]
3-8 mmHg - average increase in systolic blood pressure [25]
2-14 mmHg - average increase in diastolic blood pressure [25]
15-20% - high school students reporting serious suicidal thoughts (requiring vigilance for comorbid depression) [26]

items: Baseline measurements of blood pressure, heart rate, height, and weight plotted on growth percentiles [27]
Thorough cardiac family/personal history screening for sudden cardiac death, syncope, or arrhythmias [27]
Routine pre-treatment ECG is not mandatory for healthy, asymptomatic children without cardiac risk factors [27]
Dampening or tracking of vital signs, height, and weight at every follow-up visit [28]
Periodic complete blood count (CBC) recommended for long-term Dexmethylphenidate due to rare leukopenia/anemia risk [28]
key_numbers: 1 to 4 weeks - visitation frequency recommended during dose titration phase [28]
3 to 6 months - מעקב frequency for patients on a stable maintenance dose [28]

items: weekly titration: start at lowest dose and increase weekly until optimal response is achieved with minimal side effects [29]
Ritalin LA / Metadate CD: capsules can be opened and beads sprinkled on applesauce [8]
Concerta: OROS osmotic pump tablet, contraindicated in patients with severe GI narrowing/obstruction [8]
Daytrana: transdermal patch worn on hip for 9 hours; risk of skin irritation or chemical leukoderma [8]
Jornay PM: taken at bedtime with a delayed-release coating of 8-10 hours to target morning impairment [8]
Cotempla XR-ODT: orally disintegrating tablet, useful for patients with dysphagia [8]
key_numbers: 10-12 hours - duration of effect for Concerta, Vyvanse, and Jornay PM [8, 30]
16 hours - duration of action of Adhansia XR [8]
3-4 hours - duration of effect of immediate-release Ritalin/Methylin [8]
9 hours - maximum wear time for Daytrana transdermal patch [8]
8-10 hours - delayed-release lag time before Jornay PM begins active absorption [8]

high_yield: Pubertal shift: hepatic metabolism slows at puberty, potentially causing sudden toxicity from previously stable stimulant doses [31]
Fragile X Syndrome: stimulants are first-line for ADHD but have lower effect sizes and higher rates of side effects like irritability [32]
Prader-Willi Syndrome: stimulants treat ADHD and temporarily suppress hyperphagia to assist with weight management [32]
ADHD vs Bipolar: ADHD is chronic/continuous, Bipolar is episodic; ADHD has resistance to sleep, Bipolar has decreased need for sleep [33]
Kowatch algorithm: in comorbid mania and ADHD, prioritize stabilizing the manic episode first before initiating stimulants [26]
Zombie effect: a flat, dull, over-focused affect indicates stimulant overdosage (high DAT occupancy) rather than depressive comorbidity [26]
